learning_objective: 🎯 Learn the fundamental skills of working with different materials like wood and metal, the tools used, and the importance of safety!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Shaping materials means taking raw items (like a log of wood or a sheet of metal) and cutting, bending, or joining them to make a useful product (like a chair or a gate).
The skill of making objects out of wood. It involves measuring, sawing (cutting), planing (smoothing), and joining wood using nails, screws, or glue.
Metal is harder than wood. Shaping metal involves cutting it with heavy machines and joining pieces together by melting them at high heat (Welding).
Hand tools are operated by human muscle (like a hammer or hand saw). Power tools run on electricity or batteries (like a power drill or electric cutter) and work much faster.
Shaping materials can be dangerous. Workers MUST wear personal protective equipment (PPE) like safety goggles, thick gloves, and welding masks to prevent injuries.

fun_activity.title: 📦 Cardboard Carpentry
fun_activity.instructions: Take an empty cardboard box. Using a ruler, draw a perfect 5cm x 5cm square. Cut it out safely with scissors. You just practiced measurement, marking, and cutting—the basics of shaping!

exam_tips: 📌 Measurement is the most important step! 'Measure twice, cut once' is the golden rule.
📌 Distinguish between carpentry tools (saws, chisels) and metalworking tools (welding torch, grinders).
📌 Always list PPE (Personal Protective Equipment) when asked about workshop safety.
quick_recap: ⭐ Shaping involves subtracting material (cutting) or adding material (joining).
⭐ Planing is the process of making a rough wooden surface completely smooth.
⭐ Welding uses extreme heat to melt two pieces of metal so they fuse into one solid piece.
